hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 1}f(x)$ represents the limit of $f$ as $x$ approaches $1$.

Although the function isn't defined at $x=1$, the $y$-values seem to approach a distinct value as the $x$-values approach $1$.

![The graph of function f has arrows pointing along the curve, up to the right and down to the left, respectively, to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/b3d1f2bc49732c61b1e9b0385d0eb9b3f1373376)

The limit seems to be about halfway between $y=-5$ and $y=-4$.

![The graph of function f has a dashed horizontal line intersecting the open circle, midway between y = negative 4 and y = negative 5.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/6aace0655e4b406a28f7e7b74b30ca62ab1340b3)

question.content:
The function $f$ is defined for all real numbers except for $x=1$.

![Function f is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve. The curve starts in quadrant 3 and moves upward through an open circle at x = 1, midway between y = negative 4 and y = negative 5. The curve ends in quadrant 1.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/7bae2216e7a769a4facca26b25fbd97a28c44295)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 1}f(x)$ ?**
